The first time I saw the ocean, I was six years old. My family had driven to the coast for a weekend getaway, and I remember standing on the warm sand, staring at the endless blue horizon. The waves crashed against the shore, and I felt something shift inside me—something small but profound. I didn’t know it then, but that moment would shape how I saw the world.

Years later, I still find myself drawn to water. There’s something about its unpredictability, its quiet power, that fascinates me. It’s always moving, always changing, yet it never seems hurried. It reminds me that life doesn’t have to be rushed. Sometimes, the best things happen when you slow down and just *be*.

I’ve also learned that the ocean, like life, is full of contradictions. It can be both gentle and fierce, serene and stormy. It gives life—through rain, through the oxygen we breathe—and yet it can take it away just as easily. There’s a humility in that, a reminder that we’re not in control.

Now, whenever I’m near water, I take a moment to breathe. To listen. To remember that the world is vast, and I’m just a small part of it. Maybe that’s why I love the ocean so much—it puts things into perspective.

And if I ever feel lost, I know where to go. Back to the water. Back to the place where everything feels a little clearer.
